catalog_quote: Waja has two tonemes: high (H) and low (L). As result of 'pausal lowering',4 an additional non-high (NH) surfaces lexically. Tone-bearing units (TBU) are vowels and syllabic consonants. Falling tones (H-L) are H + L linked to one TBU. ... The major function of tone-marking in Waja is grammatical. Only a few nouns are lexically differentiated by tone (cf. (1); tonal contrast between verb stems likewise results predominantly from inflection/derivation. ... Tonal contrasts mark aspect and mood (cf. Table 39.2) and valence on verbs (4); tone distinguishes noun class pronouns and suffixes (cf. Table 39.3), and direct and indirect object pronouns. ... Several grammatical morphemes are associated with a floating tone which links within the phrase to a following morpheme, as in (6), with the floating H of the imperfective -rɛ´. ... new_statements.rule_in_words: Waja is described purely as a two-tone (H/L) language with pausal lowering, floating tones and downstep; neither the 2020 handbook chapter nor (per full-text search) the 1991 grammar contains any statement on word stress or accent placement. The 1991 grammar (p.65, snippet) says the same in German: 'Die Sprache besitzt zwei Toneme: Hoch (H) und Tief (T).'
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal notes: utterance-initial H is deleted/lowered in citation forms (1991: 'ein H auf der ersten Silbe in dieser Position in der Regel ausfällt oder abgesenkt wird', p.67 snippet), so citation forms under-represent lexical tone.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone realizations are described relative to pause/phrase position (pausal lowering at both utterance edges). Variety described: Wu lect of Dɔŋ/Talasse (the chapter states this on p.507).
new_statements.identity_note: Both Kleinewillinghöfer sources describe the Wu (plains) lect of Waja as spoken in Dɔŋ/Talasse (Gʋrsaɩ); the other main dialect is Deri (nyan derúwò) on the Longuda plateau. Glottolog waja1259 has no dialect-level codes; ISO wja.

sources.note: Sec. 39.2 Phonology = 39.2.1 Consonants, 39.2.2 Vowels (ATR harmony, length), 39.2.3 Tone: 'Waja has two tonemes: high (H) and low (L)' plus surface non-high from pausal lowering, TBU = vowels and syllabic consonants, tone mainly grammatical, floating tones, downstep. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in pp. 506-520 (in-volume search for 'stress'/'accent' returns no hits in the chapter).
